items.title: Freeze interfaces: manifests, Rational qty core, shared types, DB schema, tokens, sqlite smoke
items.acceptance: All downstream modules can import a frozen contract surface — Rational quantity type, recipe/step/score-breakdown/cooking-event shapes, household-scoped DB helpers over a real SQLite file, and the design tokens — with the repo typechecking strictly and running .ts directly on Node 24 with zero runtime dependencies.
items.notes: Runs ALONE; owns the manifests (sole exception to the manifest exclusion). Invariant 1: Rational (bigint num/den) is the ONLY arithmetic type on authoritative paths, qty.ts the sole entry point, rounding once at display/package boundary. Invariant 2: cooking-event shape stores timers as absolute UTC end instants, never remaining-seconds. Invariant 3: every db.ts helper takes household_id as REQUIRED first argument and appends the WHERE itself — an unscoped query must be inexpressible. Schema includes a separate never-overwritten column for user grocery-quantity edits [steal C]. tsc --noEmit is the gate, never a build step; devDependency typescript only. Smoke check proves node:sqlite on a real file DB with the actual statement API. tokens.css: type scale, 4px grid, dark-first verified contrast, 44px targets, focus states, prefers-reduced-motion, tabular-nums.

items.title: Build units, ingredient normalization with aliases, and curated ingredient conversion tables
items.acceptance: Ingredient text variants (including the garlic alias family: 'garlic cloves', 'cloves of garlic', 'fresh garlic', '3 cloves garlic, minced') normalize to one canonical ingredient id with a confidence value, and same-dimension conversions land in grams/millilitres/count while cross-dimension conversion happens only via curated density or per-item weight and is otherwise reported separately, never guessed.
items.notes: Invariant 1 binds: all arithmetic through qty.ts Rational; review greps for bare +/* on numbers in these files. 'To taste' is a distinct non-numeric state, never foldable into a quantity. Ranges preserved as min/max, scaled independently. CYCLE 6 (D-9): domain/src/ingredients.ts CUT — catalog.ts already owns the curated registry; a second table would be a second source of truth.

items.title: Build serving scaling and cross-recipe aggregation with full line-level traceability
items.acceptance: Requirements from multiple recipes scaled to target servings merge into single lines only when canonical ingredient id AND base-unit dimension match, every aggregated number carries links back to each contributing recipe line and amount, and the four garlic alias fixture forms produce exactly one aggregated line.
items.notes: Invariant 1 binds: Rational only, no floats. Scale factor = target_servings / servings_default applied to min and max independently. Differing preparation states preserved on the line, never silently merged. Traceability is a data structure produced here, not a UI afterthought — DoD 5's test asserts these links exist for every line.

items.title: Build confidence-gated inventory subtraction and package selection with surplus math
items.acceptance: purchase_requirement = max(0, aggregated − usable_inventory) subtracting only confirmed/assumed_staple entries (less-certain entries become confirmation-question objects, never silent subtractions), and the chosen package combination's total yield always covers the requirement — underbuying impossible — minimising (expected waste, package count), with expected_surplus computed and generic fallbacks ('one bunch', 'one ~2 lb package') flagged as estimates.
items.notes: Invariant 1 binds: Rational only; rounding once at the package boundary. Ranges purchased conservatively (against max). Surplus is a value returned for write-on-purchase-confirmation, not written here (domain stays pure). Confirmation questions are high-value and few, never a pantry review. || CYCLE 9 VERIFIED DONE. Conductor gate SWARM/runs/cycle-009-gate-T004.mjs: 22/22. The package search was checked against an INDEPENDENT conductor-written brute-force oracle over 240 (requirement, option-set) pairs across 4 package grids - zero coverage violations, zero (waste, count) mismatches, surplus exact on every probe. The subtraction formula was asserted as an identity over all 1,681 (required, on-hand) pairs in 0..40. Confidence gate probed at four magnitudes per confidence level: `inferred` never subtracts, confirmed/assumed_staple always do. Mutation gate 8/9 (SWARM/runs/cycle-009-mutate-T004.mjs); the one survivor is a test-coverage gap, not a module defect - filed as T-035.

items.title: Build attribute-level preference model, feedback updates, and variance-selecting calibration
items.acceptance: Every calibration reaction and post-meal feedback event updates per-attribute signals (protein, cuisine, flavour, texture, spice, richness, method, effort) each carrying value, confidence and durability — never one opaque score — with negative signals weighted more strongly and faster than weak positives, and the calibration module deliberately SELECTS 8–15 cards for maximum attribute spread rather than sampling randomly.
items.notes: Card selection variance is why candidate B won — the spec demands deliberately varied cards, not just reactions. Four reactions: looks good / not for me / never recommend / too much work; 'never recommend' feeds the hard-exclusion set consumed by filters. Persisted score/signal values go through Rational on authoritative paths (Invariant 1). || CYCLE 8 VERDICT: FAILED VERIFICATION (attempt 1). Gate SWARM/runs/cycle-008-gate-T005.mjs scored 44/45; the module is 95% right (asymmetry proven from EQUAL raw inputs and pinned to the exact 3/2 config ratio, all 8 axes covered, clamping exact, greedy selection beat the BEST of 500 random samples on coverage 34 vs 34 and the mean 28.97, deterministic under input reordering). The ONE failure is a product-breaking integration defect and it is the whole reason this item is not done: applyCalibrationReaction(never_recommend) writes value -1 / confidence 1 to EVERY attribute-value pair on the card (all 6 single axes plus every flavour and texture tag), and filters.ts treats ANY signal at value <= -4/5 with confidence >= 1/2 as an ABSOLUTE hard exclusion. Measured: one never_recommend tap on a chicken/thai card left 2 of 6 survivors in a catalog sharing NO protein and NO cuisine with it - r-01 and r-06 died on richness=rich + effort=high, r-02 on method=stir_fry, r-03 on spice=hot. On a real 30-recipe catalog this plausibly empties the plan and breaks DoD 2 (>=2 of 3 meals approvable) from the very first onboarding flow. FIX DIRECTION (do NOT rebuild the module - it is good work; this is a targeted change): never_recommend must not write an absolute-exclusion-strength value to GENERIC axes. Either scope the -1 lock to the distinctive axes only (protein, cuisine, and flavour tags) and write an ordinary strong negative to the generic ones (spice/richness/method/effort/texture), or introduce a recipe-scoped exclusion instead of an attribute-scoped one. Whichever is chosen, the re-verify gate will re-run the 6-recipe integration probe and require a majority to survive. The builder itself flagged this in its return as worth a second look - credit to it for the honesty. See also KI-5. || CYCLE 9 VERDICT: FAILED VERIFICATION AGAIN (attempt 2) -> BLOCKED. Gate SWARM/runs/cycle-009-gate-T005.mjs scored 14/16. What the attempt DID fix, verified: the cycle-8 defect is gone. The builder scoped the -1/confidence-1 lock to protein + cuisine + flavour and routed the generic axes (spice, richness, method, effort, texture) through the ordinary raw/multiplier path at value -9/10, confidence 2/5 - below filters.ts's 1/2 confidence gate, so no generic axis is a one-tap veto. The verbatim cycle-8 probe went from 2/6 survivors to 6/6. never_recommend stays genuinely binding (reacted card, same-protein and same-cuisine recipes all still excluded), is strictly stronger and more durable than not_for_me on every pair, and two taps sharing a generic axis still escalate it to a hard exclusion, so the model still learns. Asymmetry, clamping and calibration selection all survive intact. WHAT STILL FAILS, and why the item is blocked: the over-exclusion did not disappear, it MOVED to the flavour axis. FlavourTag contains genuinely generic members ('savoury', 'mild', 'fresh'), so locking flavour tags as 'distinctive' reproduces the same product-breaking failure. Measured on a realistic 12-recipe catalog carrying 'savoury' on 8 of 12: ONE never_recommend tap on a savoury+spicy chicken/thai card left 3 of 12 survivors, with 8 recipes excluded on `strong_dislike:flavour=savoury` alone. That still plausibly empties the plan and still breaks DoD 2. IMPORTANT ATTRIBUTION: the builder followed the fix direction in these notes verbatim, and flagged this exact risk unprompted in its return, naming the one-line remedy and explaining that it declined to deviate on an unmeasured hypothesis. That was the right call and the failure is in the cycle-8 SCOPING (mine), not in the build. The remedy is now MEASURED, not hypothesised - see T-034 and SWARM/runs/cycle-009-remedy-probe.mjs. The code is COMMITTED rather than reverted because it is strictly better than the cycle-8 state: defect A is fixed and only defect B remains. See KI-5.

items.title: Build absolute hard filters and configurable weighted scoring with persisted breakdowns
items.acceptance: Allergies, dietary restrictions, explicit exclusions, hard time ceilings and recent-repeat constraints eliminate recipes absolutely before any scoring, and survivors receive a score of 0.32 preference + 0.20 context/interruption + 0.16 inventory + 0.12 cost + 0.10 novelty + 0.10 leftover-usefulness minus explicit penalties, with weights in one config object and a full per-recipe breakdown persisted.
items.notes: Hard-constraint precedence is absolute and never averaged: allergy > household hard restriction > member hard restriction > strong dislike > soft preference > optimisation. A strong dislike can never be outweighed by inventory use or cost. Adjacent novelty = attribute distance with at least one familiar anchor preserved. No LLM anywhere. Invariant 1 binds on persisted scores. CYCLE 6: builder was killed mid-wave before writing tests/score.test.ts; behaviour verified by the conductor gate instead, and the missing regression tests are filed as T-029.

items.title: Build greedy set-scoring planset and frozen-context swap
items.acceptance: The planset pass optimises the SET of three meals for ingredient overlap, protein and cuisine diversity, total weekly active time and cost, and a swap by explicit reason (faster, less hands-on, fewer dishes, cheaper, more familiar, more adventurous, no pasta, different protein, use what I have) returns at most three alternatives ranked against the two untouched meals — which are provably unchanged.
items.notes: Invariant 4 binds and is the whole point: swap re-ranks against the FROZEN remaining two meals and NEVER re-runs planset. An agent who 'helpfully' re-optimises the set breaks DoD 3. Greedy set pass per D-2 (combinatorial search is a non-goal tonight). || CYCLE 10: dispatched but its builder produced ZERO files before the conductor session hit the account session limit (KI-6). attempts deliberately LEFT AT 0 — the build never ran, so there is nothing to escalate and nothing to penalise. Still the top critical-path pick. || CYCLE 11: BUILT AND VERIFIED. Conductor gate SWARM/runs/cycle-011-gate-T007-rev2.mjs, 58/58 (.swarm/runs/cycle-011-verify-T-007-rev2.txt). Invariant 4 proven twice: structurally (swap.ts names planset nowhere outside doc comments; no dynamic import) and in RANKING (a candidate echoing only the outgoing meal's exclusive ingredients scores overlap 0, identical to a fully disjoint candidate, while a candidate echoing a FROZEN meal scores 1 — the term is live AND correctly scoped). 27/27 slot x reason swaps returned the two untouched meals as the SAME OBJECT REFERENCES. All nine reason promises re-derived from raw Recipe fields, zero broken. Greedy set score 0.7712 vs naive top-3 0.5186 on the real catalog, and the chosen set DIFFERS from naive (so the set pass is actually exercised).

items.title: Build catalog validation gate, ingredient registry, and allergen-class cross-check
items.acceptance: A recipe is ineligible for recommendation unless quantities are complete, steps ordered, servings known, dietary tags verified, and all nine per-step interruption-metadata fields present — and every recipe ingredient id resolves in the registry with its allergen classes consistent with the recipe's dietary tags, so an allergen can never hide behind an unverified tag.
items.notes: FROZEN CONTRACT (cycle 3, T-001 landed): the nine per-step interruption fields on RecipeStep in domain/src/recipe.ts use two names that DIFFER FROM SPEC.md — `maximum_pause` (a MaximumPause union: {kind:'bounded',seconds} | {kind:'unlimited'}), NOT `maximum_pause_seconds`; and `timer_duration_seconds` (number | null), NOT `timer_duration`. Also `recovery_instruction` is a RecoveryGuidance union ({kind:'instruction',text} | {kind:'none_available'}), not a bare string. Validate against the TYPES, not against the SPEC's field names. Invariant 5 binds: this gate and the ingredient-id/allergen-class cross-check land BEFORE any recipe is authored — otherwise DoD 9 fails via data at 5am. Registry carries curated aliases, densities, per-item weights, allergen classes, store sections. The gate excludes incomplete recipes rather than failing the build, which is what makes a short catalog a graceful degradation.

items.title: Author proven first recipe batch (6 recipes, maximum attribute spread)
items.acceptance: Six recipes spanning distinct proteins, cuisines, methods and effort levels pass the full validation gate including complete quantities against registry ids, the full attribute vector, and all nine interruption-metadata fields on every step — establishing the schema-first authoring pattern the bulk batches copy.
items.notes: FROZEN CONTRACT (cycle 3): author every step against domain/src/recipe.ts RecipeStep, NOT against SPEC.md's field names. Two differ: `maximum_pause` is a union {kind:'bounded',seconds:n} | {kind:'unlimited'} (NOT `maximum_pause_seconds`), and the timer field is `timer_duration_seconds: number | null` (NOT `timer_duration`). `recovery_instruction` is {kind:'instruction',text:'...'} | {kind:'none_available'} — a real step-specific instruction or the explicit none, never a fabricated string. All nine fields are required on every step. This batch is the template: schema-first data entry against the gate, not prose. Recovery instructions must be real and step-specific (Invariant 6 consumes them verbatim). Owns numeric prefixes r01–r06 only. Include at least one very-low-effort and one adventurous recipe so calibration and swaps have range even if bulk batches slip. || CYCLE 11: BUILT AND VERIFIED. Conductor gate SWARM/runs/cycle-011-gate-T009.mjs, 37/37 (.swarm/runs/cycle-011-verify-T-009.txt). 35 steps across 6 recipes carry all 11 required interruption keys, well-typed; zero SPEC.md-era field names (D-7 held). Spread measured, not claimed: 6 distinct proteins / 6 cuisines / 6 methods, effort+spice+richness+cost all spread, 9 distinctive flavour tags. Allergen truth RE-DERIVED independently through the registry: zero contradicted dietary tags, zero undeclared allergens, 79/79 ingredient lines resolve. Metadata coherence probes passed (no continuous-attention step is pause-safe-during; 22/22 recovery instructions unique and substantive; declared active/total equal the step sums).

items.title: Build cooking session state machine with absolute-instant timers and kill-safe event log
items.acceptance: A cooking session reconstructed purely from its persisted events at any later wall-clock time yields the correct current step, elapsed/remaining timer state, next safe stopping point, and continuous-attention warnings — with recovery guidance drawn only from per-step metadata and an explicit 'unavailable' state when metadata is absent.
items.notes: Invariant 2 binds: timers are absolute UTC end instants, never remaining-seconds — recovery is arithmetic, not bookkeeping, which is what makes DoD 7 provable. Invariant 6 binds: recovery/panic guidance reads required per-step metadata only, never fabricated. Pure domain: no I/O, no Date.now() inside logic (time is a parameter).

items.title: Build prep-plan derivation, reason-code copy module, and shared total-vs-active time renderer
items.acceptance: For any valid recipe, prep derivation yields ingredients to retrieve, equipment, do-ahead tasks, the first non-interruptible step, the first safe stopping point and expected active-time blocks; and every human-readable time or reason string in the product is produced by this one module with numeric slots, always rendering total and active time as separate values.
items.notes: [Steal C] binds: ONE copy module + ONE shared time renderer makes DoD 6 a property of a single helper instead of a per-screen convention, and a voice review a one-file diff. Copy is concrete and countable ('22 min total, 7 hands-on'), guilt-free, honest about uncertainty. At most three reason codes per meal, rendered as concrete copy. || CYCLE 8 VERDICT: DONE. Conductor gate SWARM/runs/cycle-008-gate-T013.mjs 94/94, mutation gate 8/9 (D-12 method). Built prep.ts (184) + reasons.ts (293) + 624 lines of tests. Invariant 6 proven both ways: authored instruction renders verbatim, none_available renders the one honest absence sentence, and NO fabricated-guidance literal exists anywhere in the copy module (a mutant that replaced the absence copy with invented guidance was killed). DoD 6 is now structurally a property of one helper: renderTotalActiveTime always returns both sides and refuses an impossible pair (active > total).

items.title: Build HTTP server, all routes, and entrypoint with ephemeral-port and db-path flags
items.acceptance: Every product flow (onboarding, calibration, plan, swap, grocery list with preserved user edits and confirmation questions, purchase confirmation writing surplus, prep, cooking session events, feedback, cooked-decrement) is reachable over HTTP as thin routes over domain functions, and the entrypoint accepts port and db-path flags so a test can run it on a temp DB and free port.
items.notes: Invariant 3 binds: all data access through db.ts household-scoped helpers — routes must be unable to express an unscoped query; never inline SQL in routes. User grocery edits go to the separate never-overwritten column; regeneration must not clobber them by construction. Inventory decremented on 'cooked', never 'planned'. [Steal A]: the port/db-path flags are the stated mitigation for kill-test flake — they are first-class, not debug leftovers. node:http only, zero deps.

items.title: Build web shell, shared UI components, onboarding, and calibration screens
items.acceptance: A new user completes household setup (size, restrictions, allergies, never-recommend, proteins, cuisines, time ceilings, novelty, staples) and 8–15 four-reaction calibration cards in a one-handed, under-four-minute mobile flow with one dominant bottom-anchored action per screen and never more than three choices anywhere.
items.notes: Identity contract binds: tokens-only CSS (app.css consumes tokens.css, no free-hand values); ui.js is the SOLE source of shared components — bottom sheet, undo snackbar (undo everywhere, never a confirmation modal), aria-live timer announcer, reason chips, status-beyond-colour badges. Framework-free vanilla JS. Wave-2 parallel siblings consume ui.js — keep its component API small, boring, and stable.

items.title: Build plan screen with reasoned three-alternative swap flow
items.acceptance: The plan screen shows three dinners each with name, total AND active time separately, interruption profile, effort, at most three concrete reason codes, owned/shared ingredients, cost band and novelty indicator — and swapping one meal by explicit reason takes at most three taps, offers at most three alternatives, and visibly leaves the other two meals untouched. ADDED cycle 13: the screen MUST render the plan response's `shortfall` explanation when `is_empty` or `is_partial` is true — T-041 made the API honest, but conductor-verified at cycle 13 that NO web file reads shortfall/is_empty/is_partial, so today the explanation reaches no user. A plan screen that renders an empty list with no reason re-creates KI-7 at the UI layer.
items.notes: All time strings and reason copy come from the domain reasons/time-renderer module — never hand-rolled here (DoD 6 mechanism). Consume shared components from ui.js per the identity contract; do not create local variants. Builds against the wave-0 route contracts; any needed contract change is an emergency single-agent commit per the contract-drift rule. Cycle 13: shortfall copy is fully rendered by domain/src/reasons.ts — read it from the response, never re-word it here.

items.title: Build grocery list screen as a ledger with provenance drawers and protected user edits
items.acceptance: The grocery list renders grouped by store section with tabular numerals, every line expands to answer 'why am I buying this?' by naming each contributing recipe and amount, inventory deducted and expected surplus, estimated packages are labelled estimated, inventory confirmation questions surface inline, and a user-edited quantity visibly survives list regeneration.
items.notes: Receipt/ledger treatment [steal C]: typography does the trust-building the traceability must-have exists for. User edits live in the separate column — the UI reads and preserves it, never writes generated values over it. Quantity edit gets an undo snackbar from ui.js, not a confirmation modal. Honest uncertainty: 'estimated' stated plainly. CYCLE 14: 11 of 12 conductor gate checks PASSED (all 7 sections + all 22 lines render; DoD 5 provenance 29/29 line->recipe links readable; inventory deduction 2/2; user edit survives regeneration and is displayed). The ONE failure is R21: quantities render as raw rationals, e.g. "Olive oil 44 12376473/25600000 ml". Root cause is a single call site - api.js formatQuantity() only rounds when passed {maxFracDigits}, and grocery.js omits it. Do NOT rebuild the screen; fix the formatting and re-run .swarm/runs/cycle-014-gate-rev2.mjs. | CYCLE 23 VERIFIED DONE. Conductor authored a fresh 18-check gate (.swarm/runs/cycle-023-gate-T-017-rev2.mjs, never seen by any builder, expectations derived from the live wire at run time) against the FULL acceptance sentence, not just the R21 clause cycle 14 failed on. Result 15 PASSED / 0 FAILED / 3 NOT RUN. Evidence cycle-023-verify-T-017-rev2-run2.txt. R21 is dead: no raw rationals anywhere in list, drawer, or post-edit re-render (T-052 fixed it at cycle 15; nobody had re-run T-017 since). Provenance drawer names 1/1 contributing recipes and renders 1/1 amounts; inventory deduction stated in words AND numbers; quantity editor reachable; user edit visibly survives a full regeneration on a separate column (edited 1234 shown, generated 18.48 not shown as the buy amount); tabular figures confirmed via app.css .num rule applied to the rendered quantity node. THE 3 NOT-RUN CHECKS ARE UNREACHABLE-BY-DESIGN, NOT DEFECTS OF THIS SCREEN, and are reported as not-run: (a) inline confirmation questions require an inferred inventory entry and the only HTTP write path (assumed_staples) stores confidence assumed_staple, which subtracts and never asks - unreachable by D-2 confirmed-only inventory; (b) estimated-package labelling and (c) expected surplus both need package options, and data/ingredients.json ships ZERO for all 97 ingredients - filed as T-065.

items.title: Build two-tap post-meal feedback screen
items.acceptance: After cooking, a user records make-again / it-was-fine / not-again plus one optional reason in at most two taps and under five seconds, with the recorded reaction reflected in stored attribute-level preference signals.
items.notes: One dominant action; the optional reason is a second tap at most, never a form. Guilt-free copy from the shared copy module. No streaks, no engagement mechanics of any kind.
items.verify_note: cycle-016-gate-rev2.mjs 33/33 (conductor-authored post-freeze). Server-side ground truth read from the live sqlite file: one tap and nothing else wrote exactly 1 feedback row (make_again, reason null, correct recipe_id) and moved 11 preference_signals rows; verdict+reason wrote exactly 1 row (not_again / too_much_work); a revisit wrote no second row; a finished cooking session reaches the screen via a How did it go? action that lands on #/feedback/<plan_meal_id> and renders. suite 355/355.

items.title: Build interruption-aware cooking mode with resume-into-session recovery
items.acceptance: Cooking mode shows one large-text step at a time with one-handed completion, labelled active vs unattended intervals, timers rendered from stored absolute end instants, an explicit warning (with the required uninterrupted duration) before any continuous-attention step, and the next safe stopping point always visible — and reopening the app mid-session after a reload lands the user back on the correct step with timer state intact, showing validated recovery guidance from step metadata or an honest no-guidance-available line.
items.notes: Invariant 2 binds: render timer state from stored absolute UTC end instants vs now — never count down a local variable as truth. Invariant 6 binds: recovery text comes only from per-step metadata; absent metadata is stated, never fabricated. Prep screen shows retrieve/equipment/do-ahead, first non-interruptible step, first safe stopping point, active-time blocks. Build accessibility in from the start (aria-live announcer from ui.js, 44px targets); the wave-3 a11y pass does not touch these files. CYCLE 15: SPLIT — prep screen carved out to T-057 so cooking mode gets a full builder. Scope now includes router.js/index.html wiring (this item owns those files this wave) and a plan.js entry affordance into cooking. CYCLE 15: DONE — verified by cycle-015-gate-rev2.mjs, 32/32 against a live server and a real DOM. Invariant 2 proven by remounting the screen from scratch 3.2s later and watching the clock fall 3s (5:00 -> 4:57), which a stored-duration countdown cannot do.

items.title: Prove kill/reload survival of cooking sessions end-to-end
items.acceptance: An automated end-to-end scenario advances a real cooking session with running timers, hard-kills the server process, restarts it against the same database file, and observes identical step progress and arithmetically correct timer state — proving DoD 7 by execution, not claim.
items.notes: Uses the entrypoint's ephemeral-port and db-path flags (temp SQLite file, free port per run) — the designed mitigation for kill-test flake. Invariant 2 is what makes the post-restart assertion pure arithmetic on absolute instants; if this test wants to compare remaining-seconds snapshots, the implementation has drifted.

items.title: Prove the full product loop end-to-end with the broadened DoD sweep
items.acceptance: One automated pass through onboarding → calibration → plan → swap → grocery → feedback demonstrates: a plan reached within the interaction budget, at least two of three meals approvable in-app, a swap changing exactly one meal, every grocery line carrying complete recipe-level provenance, total and active time present as separate values in every payload carrying a time, and feedback recorded in two interactions.
items.notes: [Steal A] binds: this is the BROADENED loop test — DoD 2 (>=2 of 3 approvable) and DoD 6 (total+active in every time-carrying payload) are explicit assertions, not incidental. Swap assertion must verify the two untouched meals are byte-identical before/after (Invariant 4's observable consequence).

items.title: Fuzz generated households against hard-exclusion leaks
items.acceptance: Across many seeded, randomly generated households with random allergies, restrictions and exclusions, zero produced plans contain a hard-excluded ingredient — checked at the ingredient-id and allergen-class level via the registry, not by recipe tag alone, with failing seeds reported for reproduction.
items.notes: Checks through the same registry cross-check path Invariant 5 forced early — DoD 9 can fail via data (allergen present, tag unverified), so the fuzz must resolve ingredients to allergen classes itself rather than trusting tags. Deterministic seeding so a 4am failure is reproducible.

items.title: Prove household isolation on every entity
items.acceptance: With two populated households, no request or query path returns another household's preferences, inventory, plans, grocery lists, cooking sessions or feedback — covering every entity type in the schema, including attempts that pass a foreign household's ids directly.
items.notes: Invariant 3 binds: the tests prove the STRUCTURE (every db.ts helper requires household_id and scopes itself), not merely the absence of leaks in happy paths — include a check that no data-access surface exists outside the scoped helpers. Enumerate entities from the schema so a later table cannot silently skip coverage.

items.title: Accessibility and voice pass across wave-2 screens
items.acceptance: Every screen has screen-reader labels on all interactive elements, respects dynamic type without breakage, meets contrast on the dark-first palette, has 44px minimum targets, conveys all status beyond colour alone, announces timers accessibly, requires no gesture-only critical action, offers undo (never a confirmation modal) for every destructive-feeling action, and all copy is concrete, countable and guilt-free.
items.notes: Deliberately excludes cook.js/prep.js (owned this wave by T-019, which builds its own accessibility in). Copy fixes go into domain/src/reasons.ts ONLY if a string lives there — if so, that is a one-file diff by design; coordinate via deps, do not fork copy into screens. Tokens-only CSS rule binds: fixes adjust tokens/app.css, never inline styles.

items.title: Add panic button to cooking mode
items.acceptance: A single always-reachable control in cooking mode tells an interrupted cook exactly what to do right now — what can wait, what cannot, and for how long — using only the current step's stored interruption metadata.
items.notes: Strictly after DoD green; independently droppable. Invariant 6 binds hardest here: panic guidance is assembled from maximum_pause_seconds, safe_to_pause_*, natural_stopping_point and recovery_instruction — never generated text. If metadata is missing the button says so honestly. DROPPED cycle 20 (hygiene): a cooking-mode panic button is not in SPEC.md must-haves or nice-to-haves — it is a design-panel extra. It waits on five items (T-020..T-024), four of them M-effort, and the weekly governor has pinned the reachable gear ceiling at 2 for the rest of the run, so it was never going to be reached. Nothing depends on it. Dropped, not deleted.

items.title: Add show-the-math drawer to the plan screen
items.acceptance: Each planned meal can expand to show its persisted score breakdown — every weighted component and penalty with its value — matching the numbers the engine actually stored.
items.notes: Strictly after DoD green; independently droppable. Renders the breakdown the spec already forces score.ts to persist — an additive leaf, no engine changes. Numbers formatted via the shared renderer, tabular-nums. DROPPED cycle 15 (hygiene): Plan-screen show-the-math drawer: DoD 5 traceability is already proven on the grocery ledger (29/29 links, cycle 14); a second math surface is duplicate value.

items.title: Add grocery list clipboard export and use-it-up surplus suggestions
items.acceptance: The grocery list copies to the clipboard as clean plain text grouped by section, and a recorded surplus ingredient surfaces as a guilt-free chip scoring its fit against upcoming plan candidates ('the leftover half-can of coconut milk fits Thursday's curry').
items.notes: Two delighters merged because both live in grocery.js (same-wave file disjointness); if time is short ship export alone and drop the useitup half. useitup.ts is a pure leaf over persisted surplus + score data; Rational arithmetic via qty.ts (Invariant 1). Guilt-free voice binds: never 'about to waste'. DROPPED cycle 15 (hygiene): Clipboard export + use-it-up: SPEC nice-to-have, not a must-have.

items.title: Add second-adult household preferences with minimum-acceptable-fit rule
items.acceptance: A household with a second adult holding independent preference signals never receives a plan containing a meal below the minimum acceptable fit for either adult, with both adults' hard restrictions treated as absolute.
items.notes: DESIGN names this FIRST TO CUT — it is the only delighter editing existing modules rather than adding a leaf. Any touched frozen type is a contract-drift emergency (single-agent commit). Member hard restriction sits in the existing precedence chain below household hard restriction, above strong dislike. DROPPED cycle 15 (hygiene): Second-adult preferences: SPEC nice-to-have, not a must-have.

items.title: Commit regression tests for score.ts (weights, breakdown arithmetic, penalties)
items.acceptance: tests/score.test.ts asserts the six SPEC weights exactly, that they sum to one, that total equals the sum of weighted components minus the sum of penalties for a fixture set, that every persisted value is a Rational, and that an injected config is honoured by every component (no inlined weight literals). Suite green.
items.notes: T-006 landed score.ts with ZERO committed test coverage: the builder was killed by the harness before it wrote this file. The conductor gate (SWARM/runs/cycle-006-gate-T006.mjs) verified the behaviour at cycle 6, but that gate is not in the repo and npm test does not run it, so a weight drift would ship silently. This item closes that hole. Do NOT copy the conductor gate; write tests from SPEC. CYCLE 7 VERIFIED: conductor mutation gate killed 11/13 mutants; all six weight literals, the sum-to-one, the recomputed total, the Rational structure check and the injected-config check are genuinely drift-catching. Two mutants SURVIVED (recent_repeat penalty amount 0.15->0.05; excessive_active_time threshold 2400->999999) because the total test reads penalties back from the engine rather than pinning the config literals. Those are outside this item written acceptance -> filed as T-031, not papered over.

items.title: Align the registry name-uniqueness key with the fold used at match time
items.acceptance: Two entries whose aliases differ only by internal whitespace (e.g. "red  onion" vs "red onion") are REJECTED by parseIngredientRegistry, with a test proving it. Uniqueness is keyed on the same folded form matchIngredient indexes on, so no alias collision can reach the match index.
items.notes: Found by the cycle-6 conductor gate (check N5d). parseIngredientRegistry keys uniqueness on name.toLowerCase(); normalize.ts keys its alias index on foldIngredientText (lowercase + COLLAPSED whitespace). An alias pair differing only in internal whitespace therefore passes the parser and then silently collides in the fold index, where last-writer-wins. LATENT, not live: gate check N4 proves the shipped 97-entry registry has no such pair, so no current behaviour is wrong. It is an authoring-time trap, and DoD 4 is exactly about duplicate lines caused by naming differences. DROPPED cycle 15 (hygiene): Registry name-uniqueness fold: internal invariant with no user-visible symptom; no reproduction on record.

items.title: Pin the six penalty amounts and the score thresholds against silent drift
items.acceptance: Mutating any one of the six penalty amounts in SCORE_CONFIG (recent_repeat 0.15, repeated_cuisine 0.06, repeated_format 0.04, excessive_active_time 0.08, dish_count 0.02, likely_waste 0.05), or either of the excessive_active_time_threshold_seconds (2400) and dish_count_penalty_cap (0.10) settings, turns the suite RED. Each is asserted as an exact Rational literal, and at least one fixture actually draws each penalty so a threshold change is observable in a total.
items.notes: Found by the cycle-7 conductor mutation gate (SWARM/runs/cycle-007-gate-T029.mjs), evidence in .swarm/runs/cycle-007-verify-T-029.txt. Root cause is specific and worth understanding before fixing: the total test recomputes weighted components from a SPEC_WEIGHTS literal declared in the test (which is why every weight mutant dies) but subtracts penalties by reading b.penalties[name] back from the engine (line ~360), so a penalty AMOUNT drift mutates test and engine in lockstep and stays invisible. Fix by pinning penalty literals the same way SPEC_WEIGHTS pins the weights. Do NOT weaken or rewrite the existing passing assertions; add to them. repeat_penalty_window_days and dish_count_free_allowance are already covered (both mutants died).

items.title: Pin prep.ts active-time block splitting against silent drift
items.acceptance: Mutating prep.ts’s active-block membership test from `active_duration_seconds > 0` to `>= 0` turns the committed suite RED. A fixture with a zero-active step between two active steps asserts EXACTLY two maximal blocks with their exact second sums, so a step that stops splitting blocks is observable.
items.notes: Found by the cycle-8 conductor mutation gate (SWARM/runs/cycle-008-mutate.mjs); evidence .swarm/runs/cycle-008-verify-mutation.txt. IMPORTANT: the BEHAVIOUR is correct - the conductor gate proved directly that a zero-active step splits blocks into two maximal runs (cycle-008-gate-T013.mjs section G). This is purely a committed-test coverage hole: no test in tests/prep.test.ts pins it, so the engine could drift silently. Add the assertion; do not change prep.ts.

items.title: Pin the calibration card floor and the signal-seeding threshold against silent drift
items.acceptance: Mutating CALIBRATION_CONFIG.min_cards from 8 to 2, or known_confidence_threshold from 3/5 to 1, each turns the committed suite RED. The 8–15 band is asserted against a catalog large enough for the floor to bind, and a fixture with signals at confidence just above and just below 3/5 proves the seeding threshold actually moves the selection.
items.notes: Found by the cycle-8 conductor mutation gate; evidence .swarm/runs/cycle-008-verify-mutation.txt. Both survivors are in calibration.ts, and both are coverage holes rather than behaviour defects: the conductor gate independently proved the 8-15 band holds and that seeding is live (a household with confident signals gets a different selection). Sequence this AFTER T-005’s re-verify lands, since that fix touches preferences.ts and may shift these fixtures.

items.title: Re-scope the never_recommend attribute lock to protein + cuisine only (flavour falls through)
items.acceptance: One never_recommend tap on a card whose flavour tags include a generic member ('savoury', 'mild', 'fresh') must not hard-exclude the catalog's other dishes carrying that tag, while the tap still absolutely excludes the reacted dish and every dish sharing its protein or its cuisine.
items.notes: Successor to the BLOCKED T-005; carries the remaining half of KI-5. The remedy is ALREADY MEASURED by the conductor, not guessed: SWARM/runs/cycle-009-remedy-probe.mjs injects never_recommend_lock_attributes = ['protein','cuisine'] through the module's own injectable config (no source edit) and measures survivors going 3/12 -> 10/12 on the same realistic catalog, with c-11 (shares protein) and c-12 (shares cuisine) both still correctly excluded. So the change is expected to be a ONE-LINE config edit plus test updates. Two things the builder must NOT do: do not drop flavour from the model entirely - flavour tags must still receive the strong durable generic negative (value -9/10, confidence 2/5) so corroborated evidence can still escalate them; and do not weaken the protein/cuisine locks to compensate. Worth ONE paragraph of judgement in the return: whether the honest long-term shape is a curated distinctive/generic partition of FlavourTag rather than dropping the axis wholesale - 'garlicky' or 'smoky' is far more dish-defining than 'savoury'. Do not build that partition tonight without saying so; the one-line fix is what unblocks DoD 2. || CYCLE 10 RESULT: landed as the predicted ONE-LINE config change (never_recommend_lock_attributes ['protein','cuisine','flavour'] -> ['protein','cuisine']) plus a rewritten module doc and 4 rewritten/added tests. Conductor gate 23/23. The builder did NOT weaken the protein/cuisine locks and did NOT drop flavour from the model — both were checked explicitly. The builder also raised the curated-partition question it was asked to raise; filed as T-036.

items.title: Pin the purchase_if_confirmed zero-clamp against silent drift
items.acceptance: Removing the max(0, ...) clamp from ConfirmationQuestion.purchase_if_confirmed in inventoryMath.ts makes the committed suite go RED.
items.notes: The single surviving mutant (M9) from the cycle-9 T-004 mutation gate (SWARM/runs/cycle-009-mutant-T-004.txt): 8 of 9 deliberate defects were caught, but a claimed inventory quantity LARGER than the line's purchase can currently produce a negative purchase_if_confirmed with no test objecting. Same class as T-031/T-032/T-033. The module itself is correct - this is a missing test pin, not a defect. Needs one case where the inferred claim exceeds the outstanding purchase.

items.title: Partition FlavourTag into distinctive vs generic members instead of dropping the axis from the lock
items.acceptance: A never_recommend tap on a dish whose flavour tags include a DISTINCTIVE member ('garlicky', 'smoky', 'umami', 'earthy', 'herby', 'tangy', 'bright', 'spicy') hard-excludes other dishes carrying that same distinctive tag, while a tap on a dish carrying only GENERIC members ('savoury', 'mild', 'fresh') still excludes nothing beyond its protein/cuisine kin. The partition is a named exported constant, not a magic list inline.
items.notes: The honest residual of T-034, recorded by the cycle-10 gate section F rather than hidden. T-034 bought correctness by dropping flavour from the lock WHOLESALE, which also gives up real precision: a tap on a smoky dish no longer vetoes other smoky dishes. Measured consequence, not a hypothesis — the gate lists the 8 distinctive tags now falling through. This is the durable shape; it was explicitly deferred, not forgotten. NOT a blocker for DoD 2, which T-034 already unblocked. DROPPED cycle 15 (hygiene): FlavourTag distinctive/generic partition: internal model refinement, invisible to the user at 30 recipes.

items.title: Re-gate T-005's calibration-variance and feedback-update surface to clear its blocked status
items.acceptance: The two halves of T-005 that the cycle-10 T-034 gate did NOT cover are proven independently: (a) the calibration module deliberately SELECTS attribute-spread cards (deliberate variance, not merely reactions), and (b) applyFeedbackEvent narrows its extra boost onto the specific attribute(s) the reason names. Both with conductor-run evidence.
items.notes: T-005 is blocked at attempts 2 and stays blocked — the churn rule is the rule and only a human un-blocks. But its BLOCKING defect (KI-5) is now closed by T-034, and its code is in main and green. What was never independently gated is the calibration-variance and feedback-narrowing surface, which the T-034 gate does not touch. This item gates exactly that, so the morning report can say which parts of T-005 are machine-checked rather than leaving the whole item under one blocked label.

items.title: Copy for the three swap no-alternatives outcomes
items.acceptance: When a swap can offer nothing, the user is told WHY in plain language — separately for an empty pool, for every candidate already being in the plan, and for no candidate satisfying the chosen reason — rather than seeing an empty list.
items.notes: Raised by the T-007 builder unprompted (cycle 11). swap.ts returns a typed SwapNoAlternativesCode (no_candidates_in_pool | all_candidates_already_in_plan | no_candidate_satisfies_reason) with honest pool counts, but reasons.ts — the SINGLE copy module — has no ReasonFact for "nothing to offer", so the code has no rendered copy. The plan screen (T-016) needs this; without it a swap that legitimately has no answer looks like a bug. reasons.ts is a frozen module, so this is a deliberate small unfreeze, not a refactor. | CYCLE 21: RE-SCOPED and PARTIALLY LANDED, gate FAILED 13/14. The item's premise was stale: routes.ts had grown a private noAlternativesMessage() with three hardcoded count-free sentences and plan.js carried a fourth copy of one of them, so the user was already told something — just in the wrong layer, in triplicate, throwing away all four SwapCounts. Landed (committed, suite green 391/391): renderSwapNoAlternatives() in reasons.ts declaring its counts/code shape locally (no swap.ts import — swap.ts already imports reasons.ts, so the back-import would be a real cycle), routes.ts delegating, plan.js fallback demoted to a generic failure line, 14 new tests. FAILS ON: all_candidates_already_in_plan at n=1 renders "All 1 recipe that could fill this slot is already in this plan." — ungrammatical, reachable (validation permits pool_size=1 fully already-in-plan, and a 6-recipe catalog with dietary filtering hits it), and user-visible in exactly the outcome this item exists to word. Fix is the n===1 branch only; do not touch the n>1 strings, which the committed tests pin. SECOND, smaller nit to fix in the same pass: the empty-pool arm renders "The catalog has 0 other recipes to offer" — the 0 is countable but stilted, and validation proves that count can only ever be 0, so the substitution is decorative; "There are no other recipes in the catalog to offer for this slot right now" says the same thing in plain English. Keep the "that's a catalog gap, not something about your preferences" clause (mutant M2 pins it). | CYCLE 23 VERIFIED DONE. Conductor gates cycle-023-gate-T-038.mjs (13/14) + cycle-023-gate-T-038-rev2.mjs (4/4) = 17/17. Both defects fixed: n===1 now renders "The one recipe that could fill this slot is already in this plan.", and the empty-pool arm renders "There are no other recipes in the catalog to offer for this slot right now — that's a catalog gap, not something about your preferences." with the reassurance clause byte-intact. The n>1 string is byte-identical at n=2, 3 and 7, and the untouched third arm still counts and agrees at n=1 and n=3. MUTATION KILLS prove the guarding tests are not vacuous: reverting defect 1 fails 1 test, reverting defect 2 fails 2, deleting the catalog-gap clause fails 2, and reasons.ts is byte-identical after mutation testing. WIRE REACHABILITY: rev1's G14 could not drive the API into a no-alternatives outcome, which was MY error, not the product's — handleSwap already filters candidates to survivors NOT in the plan, and a swap that is never accepted does not change the plan, so repeating the request can never empty the pool. The reachable route is to make survivors == planned: a VEGETARIAN household has exactly that, so candidates is empty. Live POST returns 200 with alternatives:[], none_reason no_candidates_in_pool, and a message BYTE-IDENTICAL to what reasons.ts renders — proving routes.ts delegates rather than carrying its own copy (the triplicated private copy cycle 21 found is gone for real). Suite 394/394 and tsc --noEmit clean, both run by the conductor.

items.title: Unify familiarity derivation between score.ts and swap.ts
items.acceptance: Familiarity is derived in exactly one place, so a change to what "familiar" means cannot make the novelty score and the more_familiar/more_adventurous swap reasons disagree with each other.
items.notes: Raised by the T-007 builder unprompted (cycle 11). score.ts's novelty anchor logic is not exported and score.ts was frozen, so swap.ts carries its own familiarityOf with identical eight-axis anchor semantics. Two copies of one definition is the drift shape Invariant 5 exists to prevent. LOW priority deliberately: both copies are currently correct and tested, so this is debt, not a defect — it must not outrank a screen the user can see. DROPPED cycle 15 (hygiene): Familiarity-derivation unification between score.ts and swap.ts: internal tidiness, both paths tested.

items.title: An excluded or partial plan must explain itself instead of returning silently empty
items.acceptance: POST /api/plans for a household whose hard filters leave fewer than three eligible recipes returns a typed reason code AND rendered copy naming WHICH constraint excluded the catalog (e.g. the active-time ceiling) and what the parent can change — never a bare 201 with meals: []. GET /api/plans/current must not answer "This household has no plan yet." for a household that HAS a plan which came back empty; that message is currently false. Conductor-reproduced cycle 12: .swarm/runs/cycle-012-verify-lookfindings.txt lines 4-9.
items.notes: BLOCKER. Found by the cycle-12 live-look pass and independently reproduced by the conductor.

items.title: Onboarding default time ceilings exclude the entire shipped catalog
items.acceptance: The pre-selected onboarding defaults produce a non-empty plan against the catalog as shipped. Today web/js/onboarding.js:174-175 defaults to total_time "30" (1800s) and active_time "15" (900s), while every authored recipe is 26-78 min total and 16-27 min active — so the DEFAULT first-run path yields zero meals. Either the defaults change, or the ceiling stops being an absolute hard filter, or the catalog gains genuinely fast recipes (T-010/T-011). Whichever is chosen, prove it by building a plan from the untouched defaults and getting three meals.
items.notes: Pairs with T-041 — T-041 makes the failure honest, T-042 stops it happening on the default path. Conductor-reproduced cycle 12.

items.title: Prep quantities are unscaled — they contradict the grocery list the parent shopped from
items.acceptance: GET /api/plans/:planId/meals/:slot/prep returns ingredient quantities scaled to the plan meal's target_servings, matching the grocery list for the same plan. Conductor-reproduced cycle 12 at household_size 2: grocery says 450 g chicken and 2 potatoes, prep says 900 g and 4 (cycle-012-verify-lookfindings.txt lines 22-30) — handleGetPrep calls derivePrepPlan(recipe) on the raw recipe. A test must assert prep and grocery agree for the same ingredient.
items.verified_by: conductor gate cycle-017-gate.mjs 8/8 (imports NO domain code — re-derives every expected quantity from the raw catalog JSON with its own BigInt rationals against the live HTTP endpoint) + npm test 358/358

items.title: Nothing marks a meal cooked or decrements inventory on cooking
items.acceptance: Completing a cooking session transitions its plan meal to cooked and decrements confirmed/assumed_staple inventory by what the recipe consumed, satisfying the SPEC domain rule "Inventory is decremented on cooked, never on planned". Raised unprompted by the T-014 builder: no route in the frozen contract wires this up, and recent_meals is currently approximated from feedback timestamps rather than a real cooked_at.

items.title: No package options exist, so 20 of 28 grocery lines are unbuyable fractions
items.acceptance: Every purchasable ingredient carries package options so the grocery list can state a buyable amount with the generic fallback the SPEC names ("one bunch", "one ~2 lb package", "two 15 oz cans") and label it estimated. Conductor-measured cycle 12: 20 of 28 lines are non-integer fractions with package_label null — including "1/2 count crushed tomatoes" and "473176473/64000000 ml honey" (cycle-012-verify-lookfindings.txt lines 37-41). packaging.ts and its tests are already built and waiting on this data.
items.notes: DROPPED at cycle 24 as a DUPLICATE, not as unwanted work. T-044 ("No package options exist, so 20 of 28 grocery lines are unbuyable fractions", filed cycle 12) and T-065 ("Catalog ships zero package options...", filed cycle 23) are the same defect found from two ends. Its data half was DELIVERED this cycle under T-065 (104 options across all 97 ingredients, gate D1-D6 6/6) and its live half is now tracked by T-069. Nothing T-044 asked for is lost; it is carried by T-065 + T-069.

items.title: A plan with fewer than three active meals can never be swapped out of
items.acceptance: A household holding a 1- or 2-meal plan can still swap the meals it has. Today handleSwap requires exactly three active meals and returns 409 plan_incomplete forever, so a constrained household dead-ends with no way out.
items.notes: Fixed by generalising swap arity 3 -> 1-3 in domain/src/swap.ts and dropping handleSwap's rows.length===3 gate (D-27). Gate 22/22. Residual: with 6 recipes a planner-produced short plan has an empty candidate pool, so the constrained household gets an honest 'no_candidates_in_pool' rather than choices - catalog-bound, see T-010/T-011.

items.title: Prep active_time_blocks ship no time_label, forcing the prep screen to hand-format minutes
items.acceptance: Every active_time_block carries a rendered label from domain/src/reasons.ts, so web/js/prep.js (T-019) never formats a duration itself. The single shared time renderer is the mechanism DoD 6 relies on; a block without a label reintroduces exactly the per-screen drift it exists to prevent. Recorded by the cycle-12 conductor gate as F3b (ruling D-17), filed rather than waived.
items.notes: Verified cycle 18. Conductor gate .swarm/runs/cycle-018-gate.mjs 7/7 (imports no domain code; re-derives every label from active_seconds with its own integer rounding). Mutation-checked: mutating reasons.ts minuteLabel changes the HTTP wire label (gate drops to 4/7) and turns the suite red (9 fail), so the label demonstrably flows through the ONE shared renderer rather than a route-local string. Implemented per ruling D-18: renderActiveTimeLabel() added to domain/src/reasons.ts reusing the existing private minutesOf/minuteLabel; attached at the route encode boundary via encodeActiveTimeBlock in routes.ts; the domain ActiveTimeBlock type left presentation-free. Suite 358 -> 364, typecheck clean.

items.title: Wave-2 interaction and copy fixes found by the live-look pass
items.acceptance: Three concrete defects, each fixed and each visible in the source today: (a) ui.js:318 lets a single-select chip deselect to an empty set, so onboarding.js:229 silently submits "none"/"mostly_familiar" while the screen shows nothing selected — what is shown must be what is submitted; (b) calibrate.js:181 skips the undo snackbar on the FINAL card and auto-submits, so a mis-tapped "never recommend" on the last card is permanent, breaking the product-wide undo-never-confirm rule; (c) onboarding.js:246 uses the design mantra "22 min total, 7 min hands-on - separated, always." as user-facing hint copy, where 22 and 7 correspond to nothing on screen.

items.title: Raw domain error strings reach the user verbatim
items.acceptance: Client-visible messages are plain sentences. api.js shows err.message verbatim on every screen by design, and cooking errors currently surface as "step_completed 5 at seq 5, expected 1 of 4" and "event seq 9 after terminal status completed" — reachable from a double-tap or a stale tab.

items.title: Contract gaps deferred from cycle 12
items.acceptance: Three gaps the frozen cycle-12 contract left open, each named by a builder rather than discovered later: (a) there is no server-authoritative "calibration complete" signal, so router.js relies on a client-only localStorage flag tgd.calibration_done that a new device silently loses; (b) onboarding collects no preferred proteins or cuisines although the SPEC must-have lists them, because the frozen request shape had no field; (c) GET /api/plans/current means "most recently created" rather than a real status flag, since db.ts exposes no updatePlanStatus.

items.title: Cover the mixed_constraints shortfall branch with a real HTTP test
items.acceptance: An HTTP-level test drives a household where NO single constraint is universal across the excluded recipes (e.g. an allergy excludes some, a time ceiling excludes different ones) and asserts the mixed_constraints code plus an honest per-constraint breakdown. The single/multiple branches are covered; this one is implemented and typechecked but unexercised.
items.notes: Raised unprompted by the T-041 builder as a known gap rather than claimed as covered. Needs per-recipe ingredient/allergen knowledge hand-verified against data/ingredients.json.

items.title: GET /plans/current recomputes the shortfall live while is_partial comes from stored meals
items.acceptance: is_partial/is_empty and the shortfall explanation must be derived from the SAME instant. Today is_partial comes from the persisted meal count while the shortfall is recomputed against current household state, so if the household raises its ceiling after an empty plan, GET current can report is_partial true with shortfall null. Either persist the exclusions with the plan or derive both live.
items.notes: Raised unprompted by the T-041 builder; persisting exclusions was outside its file scope. Mirrors an existing documented GAP for reason-fact reconstruction. Low user impact today, real once settings are editable.

items.title: Grocery quantities render as raw rationals a parent cannot shop from
items.acceptance: No quantity displayed on the grocery ledger contains a fraction with a denominator above 100 or a decimal longer than three places. Every amount is a number a person can act on at a shelf. Proven by cycle-014-gate-rev2.mjs check R21 going green without that check being altered.
items.notes: Conductor-found at cycle 14 by reading actual rendered output. api.js formatQuantity(q,{maxFracDigits:n}) already implements correct round-half-away-from-zero display rounding; grocery.js calls it without options and gets the exact mixed-fraction form. Pick the digits per dimension (ml/g whole numbers, count maybe 1dp) and state estimates honestly. Interacts with T-044: package options would make these numbers buyable rather than merely readable. CYCLE 15: DONE — the unaltered cycle-014-gate-rev2.mjs now passes 29/29 with R21 green (was 28/29), exactly as the acceptance demanded, AND the stronger, differently-shaped G2-G8 checks in cycle-015-gate-rev2.mjs pass on a third household shape, so the fix is general rather than tuned to R21.

items.title: renderTimeInfo drops the domain separator between total and active time
items.acceptance: The DOM text of renderTimeInfo with both fields present reads the same as the domain combined_label, separator included - not "26 min total16 min hands-on". Every screen that calls it (plan.js, calibrate.js) inherits the fix.
items.notes: Raised by the T-016 builder and CONFIRMED by conductor diagnostic at cycle 14 (.swarm/runs/cycle-014-diagnostic.txt DIAG 1: all 3 meals). aria-label is correct, and CSS gap makes it look fine, so this is not a blocker - but copy/paste, text extraction and any non-CSS rendering read the two times fused. DONE cycle 20. Conductor gate 14/14 (c20-gate-T053.mts), proven failable: the same gate scores 9/14 against HEAD ui.js. The gate never hardcodes the expected string — it asks domain/src/reasons.ts and compares byte-for-byte, so a client that renders the right words with the wrong separator still fails. items.title: Kitchen timers are unreachable — nothing in the product can ever start one
items.acceptance: Starting from a plan, a user can reach a cooking step that has a timer and start it with one tap, and the running timer then appears on the cooking screen with the correct remaining time. Proven end to end through the HTTP API and the rendered screen — never by injecting a timer_started event directly.
items.notes: Conductor-found at cycle 15 by grepping for producers of the timer_started event: there are none anywhere in web/ or in server business logic — only server/src/routes.ts:1418, the validator that would accept one. Root cause is a contract gap the T-019 builder documented in cook.js's header rather than papering over: encodeStepView (routes.ts:1239) never emits the step's timer_duration_seconds nor any has-a-timer flag, so the client cannot honestly offer 'start timer' — deriving a duration from total minus active would be WRONG for several shipped recipes, and a wrong kitchen timer is worse than none. Fix is two-sided: add timer_duration_seconds to encodeStepView, then add the one-tap start action to cook.js. Cycle 15's gate proved rendering, ticking, expiry and acknowledgement all work correctly once a timer exists (C12-C14) — this is purely the missing way IN. Same shape as T-055 (inventory confirmation questions unreachable).
items.verification: Conductor gate cycle-024-gate-T-058.mjs rev2, 15/15 (.swarm/runs/cycle-024-verify-T-058.txt). items.title: A verdict tapped and abandoned within ~2.5s can be lost on a hard tab close
items.acceptance: A verdict tapped and then abandoned by closing the tab immediately (before the screen commits) still reaches the server, or the screen stops deferring the write. Proven by a check that closes the page inside the deferral window.
items.notes: Conductor-found at cycle 16 while reading feedback.js against the gate result. The screen deliberately sends exactly ONE POST /api/feedback per visit (the server has no upsert and applyFeedbackEvent would double-count a second write - the builder documented this and it is the right call), so tap 1 does not write immediately: commit() fires on a reason tap, Done, in-app navigation cleanup, pagehide, or a 2500ms safety-net timer. Gate F6 proves the timer path works (row present within 4s). The uncovered case is a HARD close inside those 2.5s: pagehide fires but an async fetch is not guaranteed to flush. navigator.sendBeacon or keepalive:true on the pagehide path would close it. Low frequency, real data loss when it happens - not a correctness bug in what IS written.

items.title: No server-authoritative way to know a meal already has feedback
items.acceptance: Whether a plan meal already carries feedback is readable from the server (a GET, or a field on the plan meal), and the feedback screen uses it instead of localStorage. A second submission for the same plan_meal_id is refused or upserted rather than double-counted.
items.notes: Contract gap documented in feedback.js header and confirmed by the conductor at cycle 16: the feedback table has no unique constraint on plan_meal_id and there is no read path, so already-submitted is tracked in localStorage under tgd.feedback.<planMealId> - honest for one browser only, exactly the limitation tgd.calibration_done already has (KI family). Gate F14 proves the CLIENT does not double-write; nothing prevents a second device or a cleared cache from inflating a preference signal.

items.title: Garnishes are indistinguishable from essentials on the grocery list
items.acceptance: A grocery line whose every contributing recipe line is authored `optional: true` is marked as such on the wire and in the UI, so a parent can skip it knowingly. Conductor-verified at cycle 17: all six catalog recipes carry optional lines (r01 feta + flat_leaf_parsley, r02 lime + cilantro, r03 lime + red_pepper_flakes, r04 lemon + cilantro, r05 sesame_seeds + red_pepper_flakes, r06 sesame_seeds) and aggregate.ts never reads the `optional` flag, so they land on the list looking exactly as required as the chicken.
items.notes: RULING (conductor, cycle 17): do NOT drop optional lines from the list — a parent who skips buying the parsley because the app hid it still ends up without parsley. Buying them is right; presenting them as mandatory is not. The thing to fix is the missing signal. Note also that recipe.ts:79 documents `optional` as "excluded from hard requirements", which the grocery path does not honour — one of the two must change, and this item says it is the comment. The builder that surfaced this attributed the quote to SPEC.md; it is a code comment, and SPEC.md line 87 does not rule on garnishes at all.

items.title: The client re-implements the shared time renderer three different ways
items.acceptance: No file under web/ converts seconds into displayed minutes. Every duration a screen shows is a label string the server already rendered via domain/src/reasons.ts, taken verbatim. Proven by a test that fails if seconds-to-minutes arithmetic reappears anywhere in web/, plus a wire-level check that every duration a screen displays has a server-rendered label available for it.
items.notes: Found by the cycle-18 conductor second-formatter sweep while gating T-040 (evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-018-verify-T-040.txt section 5). Three distinct violations, worst first. (1) web/js/ui.js:502 builds the text inline from the raw minute count and bypasses even the client own helper, so at a sub-minute active duration it renders "0 min hands-on" where the server renders "under 1 min hands-on" — a real phrasing split inside one product, though whether the current catalog can produce a sub-minute active duration is UNVERIFIED and should be checked before assuming a user can see it. (2) web/js/ui.js:467-469 minuteText is a verbatim line-for-line reimplementation of reasons.ts:91 minuteLabel — two copies of one function in two languages, pinned against each other by nothing; they agree today by luck, not by construction. (3) web/js/cook.js:143 durationWords is a THIRD phrasing entirely ("18 minutes" where the rest of the product says "18 min"). T-040 closed this hole for prep active_time_blocks only; its acceptance was scoped to the wire and the not-yet-built prep.js, so these were filed rather than folded in. Same DoD 6 mechanism T-040 serves — the difference is that T-040 was one missing field and this is a whole duplicated renderer. CROSS-NOTE cycle 20: this item SUBSUMES T-053. T-053 is the S-effort fix to the separator + the sub-minute branch inside renderTimeInfo, landed under a gear-1 clamp; T-063 is the structural removal of every seconds->minutes conversion under web/. Whoever takes T-063 must not regress the T-053 gate: client text must remain byte-identical to the domain combined_label, including the "under 1 min" branch.

items.title: A routes test pins a catalog fixture fact that recipe batches 2 and 3 will legitimately break

items.title: Catalog ships zero package options, so package-size selection, estimate labelling and surplus are all dead code
items.acceptance: Every ingredient a catalog recipe can require carries at least one package option with a yield, and generic fallbacks are flagged is_estimate. A grocery list for a real plan then contains at least one line with a non-null package_label, at least one is_estimate line, and at least one line with non-zero expected_surplus - so the grocery screen renders the package, the estimate label and the surplus it was built to render.
items.notes:
FOUND BY THE CYCLE-23 T-017 GATE, not by a builder. domain/src/packaging.ts is fully implemented and unit-tested (package selection, integer package counts, generic-fallback is_estimate flagging, surplus arithmetic), and routes.ts encodes package_label / is_estimate / expected_surplus onto every grocery line. But data/ingredients.json carries only id, display_name, aliases, allergen_classes, store_section, density_g_per_ml, per_item_weight_g for all 97 ingredients - NO package options at all. Conductor-measured on a live 22-line grocery list for a 3-meal plan: 0 lines estimated, 0 lines with non-zero surplus, package_label null on every line checked. Consequence: three separate clauses of T-017 acceptance are unrenderable, and D-4 named package-size selection and leftover optimization as two of the three differentiators prior-art scouting found UNOCCUPIED across all five competitor products. The moat is written but has no data behind it. This is data authoring plus a validation gate, not new engine code - the engine is done. Add the catalog gate check that every required ingredient has >=1 package option so this cannot silently regress (same shape as the existing ingredient-id/allergen-class cross-check, DESIGN.md invariant 5).

CYCLE 24 GATE RESULT — 8 pass / 3 fail (.swarm/runs/cycle-024-verify-T-065.txt). The DATA half of the acceptance is DONE and proven: all 97 ingredients carry >=1 well-formed package option (104 options, 0 malformed, 0 duplicate ids), all 48 ingredient ids any shipped recipe can require resolve, and the is_estimate flag is used in both directions (32 estimated / 72 exact). The LIVE half FAILS: on a real 3-meal plan the grocery endpoint returns 22 measured lines with package_label null on 22/22, is_estimate true on 0/22 and non-zero expected_surplus on 0/22. Root cause is NOT the data: server/src/routes.ts:1125 calls selectPackages(..., [], ...) with a hardcoded empty options array, and domain/src/catalog.ts never parses a package_options field at all (grep for "package" in catalog.ts returns nothing). Both files were outside this item's file scope. CONDUCTOR SCOPING ERROR, recorded as such: I composed the wave from this item's stored files_hint (data/ingredients.json, tests/packaging.test.ts) and from its own note that "the engine is done", without checking the catalog->routes seam; routes.ts was in the concurrent T-058 builder's scope, so the wiring could not have been added this cycle in any case. The authored data is real, verified, committed value that stays. The wiring is filed as T-069, and this item is blocked on it.

VERIFIED cycle 25. The cycle-24 gate, re-run unmodified now that T-069 landed, goes 8-pass/3-fail -> 11 pass / 0 fail (.swarm/runs/cycle-025-verify-T-065.txt): L2 22/22 labelled, L3 7/22 estimated, L4 18/22 with non-zero surplus. items.title: Inventory confirmation questions are unreachable through any user-facing path
items.acceptance: Either the product exposes a write path that produces an inferred inventory entry (so confirmation questions can actually surface and the grocery screen clause is testable), or SPEC.md records explicitly that confirmation questions are out of scope for this build under D-2 and the T-017 acceptance clause is struck. One or the other - the current state, where the spec promises a surface no input can reach, is the thing to fix.
items.notes: FOUND BY THE CYCLE-23 T-017 GATE. inventoryMath.ts raises a ConfirmationQuestion only for an inferred entry against a line with a positive purchase requirement (questions subset of inferred x positive-purchase lines, per its own header comment). The ONLY HTTP write path into inventory is assumed_staples on POST /api/households, which routes.ts stores at confidence assumed_staple - and usableInventoryIds treats assumed_staple as usable, so it SUBTRACTS and never asks. D-2 deliberately cut the inference layer (confirmed-only inventory), so this is a consequence of an accepted scope cut rather than a bug. The domain logic is correct and unit-tested. RECOMMENDATION: take the spec-side branch, not the code-side one - adding an inference layer at this point reopens a cut D-2 made deliberately and the user endorsed. Prefer striking the clause and saying so plainly in REPORT.md.

items.title: Prep screen tells a parent to "Pause up to 418 minutes"
items.acceptance: A bounded maximum_pause renders in humane units — "about 7 hours", not "418 minutes" — and duration formatting lives in ONE shared place rather than a second private helper inside prep.js.
items.notes: FOUND BY THE CYCLE-23 T-057 GATE (check P9), root-caused at web/js/prep.js:182-188 durationWords() and :206-212 safeStopText(). Two things in one finding. (1) COPY: durationWords divides by 60 and stops, so a bounded pause of 25,080s renders "Pause up to 418 minutes". No parent reads 418 minutes; SPEC.md asks for concrete COUNTABLE copy, and a count nobody can hold in their head is not countable. Wants hours-and-minutes above some threshold. (2) ARCHITECTURE: this is a SECOND time-formatting path in the client. DESIGN.md grafted the single shared total-vs-active time renderer precisely so DoD 6 would be a property of ONE helper, and T-040 put time_label on the wire so screens never compute minutes themselves. maximum_pause ships raw seconds with no label, so prep.js had no local choice — which means the RIGHT fix is the wire-side one: give maximum_pause a time_label exactly as T-040 did for active_time_blocks, and delete durationWords. Prefer that over a client-side helper, for consistency with the invariant that already exists. NOT an acceptance failure for T-057 (all six required elements and the T-040 verbatim rule pass), which is why T-057 is done and this is filed separately rather than reopening it.

items.title: Prep screen copy and accessibility pass (6 findings from the cycle-23 look pass)
items.acceptance: All six findings below are fixed in prep.js: the safe-stop line no longer says "right now" on a screen shown before cooking starts; the "pause anywhere" line claims only what a null first_non_interruptible_step actually proves; the decorative "Prep plan" status badge is gone or carries a real fact; the empty state does not say "slot"; the two statically-rendered panels drop their live-region roles; and the optional-ingredients list carries a programmatic label.
items.notes:
FROM THE CYCLE-23 QA LOOK PASS — DEGRADED (browserless: no Chromium and no browse CLI on this host, so nothing below is a judgment about rendered pixels). Six findings consolidated into ONE item because they are all small edits to a single file; filing eight separate items would have pushed the live backlog past the ~30 cap for no gain. (1) SAFE-STOP TENSE, certain: prep.js:201 renders "Safe to stop right now, during step 1." — phrasing lifted verbatim from cook.js:187 where "right now" is true mid-session. On the prep screen the parent has not started cooking, so it asserts a state that is not happening. Wants a pre-cook phrasing for kind "now". (2) "PAUSE ANYWHERE" OVERCLAIM, real but LATENT — conductor-verified both ways. The agent is right that prep.ts:154-158 derives first_non_interruptible_step from requires_continuous_attention ALONE, while safe_to_pause_before/during/after and maximum_pause are independent fields (recipe.ts:117-125), so a null does NOT prove "pause anywhere". BUT the conductor also checked the shipped data: across all 35 steps in the 6-recipe catalog, ZERO steps are not-continuous-attention yet not fully pausable, so the copy is not wrong for any recipe that exists today. It becomes wrong the first time such a step is authored, and D-2 plans a 30-recipe catalog. Fix the copy to claim only what the null proves, and/or add the invariant to the catalog validation gate. Recorded as latent rather than active so nobody re-derives this at 5am. (3) DECORATIVE BADGE, certain: prep.js:446 renders a static "Prep plan" status badge restating the h1 — the rendered screen opens "PrepPrep planEverything to line up…". Elsewhere badges carry real status (cook.js "Paused", plan.js "Safe to pause anytime"); a decorative one dilutes the pattern and contradicts tokens.css's "nothing decorating harder than the numbers". (4) JARGON, certain: prep.js:428 empty state says "This slot doesn't have an active dinner in your current plan." plan.js keeps "slot" internal and says "Dinner N of 3" to users. (5) LIVE-REGION ROLES, certain: prep.js:301 and :317 put role="status" on panels rendered ONCE at mount, copied from cook.js:308,313 where those panels update during a live session (and where the attention warning is role="alert", not "status"). On static content they do nothing useful and some screen readers announce them on insertion. (6) OPTIONAL LIST UNLABELLED, certain: prep.js:242-243 introduces the optional ingredients with a bare

subhead over an unlabelled

    , so a screen-reader user navigating by list meets a second ingredient list with nothing distinguishing it from the required one — blurring exactly the must-have/nice-to-have split the code comment says must never blur. DELIBERATELY NOT FILED, with reasons: the "N count" unit rendering ("Lemons 3 count") is stilted but is the SAME convention grocery.js:334 uses, so a prep-only fix would create the cross-screen divergence this pass exists to prevent — it belongs in a shared helper or nowhere; and the raw 2px icon margins at prep.css:147,174 are pre-existing shared debt identical to cook.css:55,78 and plan.css:41, so the only accurate local fix is amending prep.css's own header comment, which currently claims "no raw px". The pass found NO token violations otherwise: every colour, size, radius and duration in prep.css is a var() token, and the section/list/warning vocabulary deliberately reuses grocery/cook/plan rather than inventing new patterns. STILL UNVERIFIED BY ANYONE (what a browser pass would need): real wrapping of long ingredient names against the nowrap quantity column, rendered contrast of the danger-bordered attention panel in both colour schemes, true 44px hit areas on a small viewport, whether six stacked sections scan as a checklist or a wall at real phone height, and screen-reader behaviour on load.

items.title: Start-timer control renders "Start NaN minutes timer" if the duration is ever absent, and its label is ungrammatical
items.acceptance: The start-timer control renders only when the step's timer duration is a positive finite number, and never renders a label containing NaN, undefined or null. Its copy reads as English a parent would say out loud.
items.notes: FOUND BY THE CYCLE-24 FAILABILITY RUN, not by a test. cook.js:573 gates the control on `step.timer_duration_seconds !== null`. Under mutant M1 (the field deleted from encodeStepView) the value is `undefined`, which is `!== null`, so the control rendered anyway with the label "Start NaN minutes timer" (cycle-024-mutants-T-058.txt). NOT a shipped defect — the field is present on every payload today, and the cycle-24 gate proves it — so this is hardening, not a bug fix: a finite-number check instead of a null check. Second, smaller point in the same three lines: the label reads "Start 35 minutes timer"; "Start 35-minute timer" is what a person says. items.title: tsconfig.web.json omits "types", so node globals typecheck inside browser code
items.acceptance: Client code referencing a node-only global (`process`, `Buffer`, `__dirname`) fails the web typecheck. Proven by injecting `process.version` into a web/js file and seeing tsc reject it — today it is ACCEPTED.
items.notes: FOUND BY THE CYCLE-25 T-054 GATE's PROBE-2, which is reported honestly rather than scored: it is outside T-054's acceptance, so it did not fail that item. The main tsconfig.json pins types: ["node"]; tsconfig.web.json omits the key entirely, which means @types/node is ambient in browser code. Measured: appending `const x = process.version` to web/js/router.js leaves `tsc -p tsconfig.web.json` at exit 0. One line — "types": [] — plus a re-run of the injection probe to prove it now rejects.

items.acceptance: No `{any}` annotation remains in web/js. Each is replaced by the real wire shape the server actually encodes (read off server/src/routes.ts's encode functions, never invented), and the web typecheck stays green.
